dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Watch your step, dear. This place is teeming with books. It'd be quite a headache if you accidentally tumbled into one of the stranger books.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: My name is Vindogeneta de Uxellobrogi.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Hard to pronounce, isn't it? It's so long that even I can't be bothered to say it. You can just go by what the Remurians do and call me "Vindia."

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Mr. Castiglione mentioned that the descendants of the High Sea would call me the "Madam Snow-Winged Goose"... but there's no need for you to use that. It makes me sound like some strange old crone.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: I was once the Queen of Uxellobrogi. As for now? I'm just an ordinary fairy tale writer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's that book over there?

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: As you can see, it's just a "storybook" that's been knocked over.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: A never-ending tea party, a clock that runs backward, talking penguins, and a princess of flowers... In short, nothing but useless fairy{RUBY#[D]fantasies}-tale.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: After all, fairy tales are written for children who refuse to go to sleep. And the children here, my dear friend, have been awake for far too long.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm leaving now.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Goodbye, dear. Watch your step, don't fall into the rabbit holes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Queen...

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Honestly, there wasn't much of a difference. When I was Queen, my only job was to smile and nod. Having nothing better to do, I spent my time penning fairy tales in secret.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Whether it was surrendering to the Remurians or to the High King{RUBY#[D]Errighenth} of Aremorica, those were decisions made by the regency elders.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: So, you see, even when that deity brought me to this place, no one actually cared.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Besides, this way, I won't be forced to go to Aremorica to pay my respects, put on a fake smile, and listen to those barbarians who don't even bathe...

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Sorry, I meant my venerable compatriots. Anyway, I'm spared from listening to them and that woman bickering endlessly over how many people they should kill. Honestly, she deserves to stay single for the rest of her life. A wonderful ending, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's that room over there?

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Oh, my dear, it would be best not to disturb him. Mr. Bickerstaff has quite the temper. Writers who wrestle with satire but can't quite finish the novel often end up like that.

dialogues.speaker: Vindia
dialogues.text: Her Majesty the High King {RUBY#[D]Errighenth} of Aremorica has more than a few such fellows in her service as well. In a sense, I suppose you could call it a kind of knightly spirit.
